subject: Math
text_verbatim: 1 Numberland Adventures: Up to 999 Explorer's Pathway 1 I can count numbers up to and across 999 (3- digit numbers) forwards and backwards, beginning from zero or one, or from any given number. 2 I can read and write numbers up to 999 in numerals and up to 99 in words. 3 I can recognise the place value of each digit in 3-digit numbers (hundreds, tens, ones/units). 4 I can compare and order numbers up to 999 using appropriate language and <, > and = signs. 5 I can round numbers to the nearest tens using different concrete objects and pictorial representations. 6 I can round numbers to the nearest tens using different concrete objects and pictorial representations. 7 I can recognise the position of objects and write it using ordinal numbers up to 20. 8 I can read and write roman numbers up to 12. 1

illustrations.description: Chapter banner: a blue rounded rectangle with an orange ribbon/bookmark tag on the left containing the white chapter number '1', and the chapter title 'Numberland Adventures: Up to 999' in white bubble-style text on the blue background.
A round blue-and-white compass icon (N/E/S/W marked, gold star centre) sitting beside the 'Explorer's Pathway' heading.

A winding light-purple/lavender path (like a ribbon road with white speed-line marks) snaking down the page in an S-shape, connecting 8 numbered star-shaped waypoints (stars numbered 1-8, each a black-outlined white star). Each star sits beside a white speech-bubble-style rounded rectangle containing one SLO (student learning outcome) statement in dark text. The road winds left-to-right then right-to-left across roughly three horizontal bands, finishing at an open treasure chest at the bottom-right.

flags: Source content duplication: SLO star #5 and SLO star #6 print the IDENTICAL sentence verbatim ('I can round numbers to the nearest tens using different concrete objects and pictorial representations.') — kept verbatim per faithfulness rule, flagged as a likely source/printing error (a distinct SLO, e.g. for hundreds rounding, may have been intended for one of the two slots).
